name: The lesson's words
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
show: insert bus, tea, team, ten, to, toast; labels()
why: ['bus', 't', 'e', 'a', 'm', 'n', 'o', 'ast']: the chains b-u-s and a-s-t became single edges. If you see one letter per edge, chains were not merged: a new word's remaining letters should go on one new edge.

name: Split an edge
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
show: the same words, then toad; labels()
why: [..., 'o', 'a', 'd', 'st']: toad leaves the edge ast after the a, so the edge splits into a (a new node) with st and d below it.

name: Word ends inside an edge
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
why: ['to', 'ast']. to ends in the middle of the edge toast: split it there and mark the new node as a word end.

name: One word
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
why: ['hello']. One word is one edge from the root.

name: Order does not matter
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
show: the lesson's words in a different order; labels()
why: The same compressed trie as the first test: ['bus', 't', 'e', 'a', 'm', 'n', 'o', 'ast'].

name: Search inside an edge
expect: [[True, False, False, False, False, False, True, False, True, False, False], [True, True, True, False, False, True, True, True, True, True, False]]
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], [T.search(q) for q in args[1]], [T.starts_with(q) for q in args[1]]][1:])(RadixTrie())
show: insert toast, tea, hello; then search and starts_with for toast, toa, to, tob, toasts, hell, hello, h, tea, te, x
why: search is True only for toast, hello and tea. starts_with is also True for toa, to, hell, h and te: a prefix may end in the middle of an edge, so compare only the part of the label that the prefix covers.

name: Inserted twice
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], T.labels()][1])(RadixTrie())
show: insert abc, abc, ab, ab; labels()
why: ['ab', 'c']. Inserting a word that is already there changes nothing.

name: 20,000 words
expr: (lambda T: [[T.insert(w) for w in args[0]], len(T.labels()), len(T.labels()) <= 2 * len(set(args[0])), sum(T.search(q) for q in args[1]), sum(T.starts_with(q[:4]) for q in args[1])][1:])(RadixTrie())
show: insert 20,000 words; [number of edges, at most 2n?, how many of 20,000 searches say True, how many of their 4-letter prefixes are found]
why: A compressed trie has at most 2n nodes. If the number of edges is much larger, chains of one-child nodes were not merged.
